bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the article's first page (PDF p. 2)
bibliography.note: Garvey, J. E., Herra, T. P. & Leggett, W. C. 2002. Ecological Applications 12(1): 194–205. PDF p. 2 = printed p. 194.

claims.claim: Lepomis larvae at Lake Opinicon were much denser in shallow open water near the colonies than offshore; at the deepest site density was 8 % of the inshore mean (Garvey et al. 2002, via Neuswanger et al. 2015)
claims.location: p. 198 (PDF p. 6), Fig. 2 caption; p. 199 (PDF p. 7); p. 201 (PDF p. 9)
claims.quote: Densities of larvae at the deep-water site were only ~8% of average inshore densities
claims.conditions: Lake Opinicon, Ontario (787 ha), 12 May–6 Aug 1998; paired 0.5-m, 500-µm surface tows twice weekly at four inshore sites (≤ 2.5 m) and one 'Deep' site in mid-lake near one of the deepest areas (8 m); bluegill and pumpkinseed larvae (< 15 mm SL) combined; deep densities 'only weakly related' to inshore (r² = 0.15)
claims.note: Now read at first hand, so 'via Neuswanger et al. 2015' can go. Garvey: 'most larvae occurring in shallow-water areas near the nesting sites' (p. 201).

claims.claim: in 1998 a cooling from 70 to 64 °F (21 to 18 °C) right after the early larval peak was followed by poor survival of early cohorts
claims.location: p. 202 (PDF p. 10); results p. 199 (PDF p. 7), Fig. 4–5
claims.quote: Water temperatures sharply declined from 21°C to about 18°C immediately following the peak
claims.conditions: late May 1998 at Lake Opinicon (QUBS 1-m water temperature record); 40 % of larvae had appeared by 12 June but most fall juveniles came from larvae produced in late June or later; survival from swim-up to the juvenile stage was often low when the swim-up temperature was below 23.5 °C
claims.note: The source is in °C ('21°C to about 18°C'); the °F pair is a conversion. Garvey offers the cooling as a possible mechanism (slower growth and longer exposure to predators, from unpublished bioenergetics runs), not a demonstrated cause.

claims.claim: pumpkinseed in northern inland lakes: ~35 mm TL first-winter threshold (Fox & Keast 1991; Garvey, Herra & Leggett 2002, both via Sobchak et al. 2026)
claims.note: Garvey et al. give no size threshold. They report that the 1998 cohort's mean total length rose from 39.3 ± 3.3 mm (6 October) to 44.5 ± 3.5 mm (11 May 1999), which 'suggests the selective loss of small individuals during winter' (p. 200), with bluegill and pumpkinseed pooled (pumpkinseed 26 % of the catch); in Fig. 8 the autumn age-0 fish start at ~31 mm. The ~35 mm figure may be Fox & Keast's, or Sobchak et al.'s reading; it should not be credited to Garvey et al.

notes: Also useful: sunfish nesting began 22 May 1998 at 19 °C; golden-eye embryos per nest 1133 ± 553 (bluegill) and 576 ± 305 (pumpkinseed), n = 5 nests each; larvae spent 2–3 weeks in open water and returned to the littoral at ~20 mm TL (citing Werner & Hall 1988); juveniles were trawled in offshore vegetation at 1–3 m in autumn; larval survival was unrelated to edible zooplankton (and higher when small zooplankton were < 100/L).
